string.text: Kill the boss yourself and the coordinates of a rare (yellow) stash on the current map come through on your PDA, filled by the game's own stash system. If the map has no free stash left, they come on the next map that has one. Default off.

Sets the hunt settings at once: grace period, time between hunts, hunt time limit, escalation, retreat health, BR mitigation, accuracy, boss chance, boss days after grace and squad size. Change any of those by hand and this shows Custom. Picking a difficulty again overwrites them. Default Medium.
Loudness of the teleport sound when a hunter breaks off or vanishes. 0 mutes it. Default 40.

A psy hum in your head while a named hunter is within 60 m: half this volume at 60 m, full volume within 10 m. A named hunter is the main Nemesis enemy: hard to kill, he retreats when hurt and comes back stronger. 0 mutes it. Default 20.
Loudness of the radio static that comes with the arrival warning. 0 mutes it. Default 70.
Radio static (for the boss also psy voices) 30 to 120 seconds before a hunt starts. With this or the PDA warning on, the hunt follows the warning; with both off it starts without one. Default on.
A PDA message from an unknown frequency 30 to 120 seconds before a hunt starts. With this or the audio warning on, the hunt follows the warning; with both off it starts without one. Default off.

On: the emission boss can come when an emission meets a hunt (see Emission boss chance). Off: he never comes, hunts during emissions are normal hunts, and one waiting to come is called off. The debug box still forces him. Default on.

Chance, rolled once per emission, that the emission boss comes when an emission meets a hunt: a hunt running when the emission starts is called off, or a hunt about to start during one is taken over. He haunts the exits of the building you shelter in, arrives with a lightning strike and walks in after you. He comes in the deadly part of the emission, when its waves hit, and never outside one. 0 turns him off. Default 100.

Chance, rolled once per emission, that the emission boss comes even when no hunt meets the emission, so between hunts too. Not in the grace period, and not while you are in a base, in a dialogue, asleep or underground. 0 turns it off. Default 4.
Name of the emission boss, a Sin (UNISG when you are Monolith, Zombified or Sin). Default: Ilarion Hrech
How much less damage the emission boss takes from other stalkers and mutants, so they are little help against him. Your own hits are not affected. Him only. Default 70.

Mutants that come through the door 15 seconds after the emission boss arrives and rush in after you: zombified stalkers, with a snork on mid maps and two tougher snorks on late maps. 0 sends none. Default 4.
The share of your whole psy bar you lose each time the ghosts at the exits shove you back inside before the emission boss arrives. Psy protection does not lower it. 0 turns it off. Default 4.
Loudness of the lightning strike when the emission boss arrives. 0 mutes it. Default 80.
Name of the Monolith boss, a rare and stronger named hunter who fights to the death. Other hunters always get random names. Default: Bogdan Kravets
Name of the UNISG boss, their best fighter, who hunts Monolith, Zombified and Sin players. Default: Lyutomyr Kat

Chance that a hunt brings the boss: a tougher, cloaked hunter with his own look and messages and an escort. It climbs by 2 every 4 hunts without him, and the 30th hunt without him brings him for sure. Only one boss at a time, at most one a day. Beating a hunt he was in halves the escalation. 0 = no boss at all. Default 2.
How much tougher the boss is than a normal named hunter. He never retreats: he fights until he or you are dead. 0 = no tougher. Default 30.

A flat amount of ballistic rating (armour class, the same scale as Extra BR cap) added to the boss's body and head armour, on top of what every named hunter gets. Not BR mitigation percent. Needs GAMMA ballistics. 0 = no extra. Default 0.

How hard the boss hits other stalkers and mutants, in percent of a normal hit. He fights anyone who fights him, but always prefers you; this makes him a killer against them. Your own damage from him is not affected. Default 200.

How many named hunters come with the boss. They hunt you like any named hunter, the real threat and distraction, while he sneaks up to finish you. A boss hunt ignores Squad of 1 to 5 and Extra is a named hunter. 0 = he comes alone. Default 4.

A gentle wave over your screen while the boss is near: it starts softly at 60 m and grows to this strength at 5 m. It works while he is cloaked too, and fades out when he dies. 0 turns it off. Default 50.
In-game days after the grace period before a boss can appear. Default 7.
Use the high definition portrait on PDA messages. Off uses the original low definition icon.

For testing: hunts start sooner (no grace period, 120 seconds between hunts, 15 seconds from the warning to the hunt) and can spawn anywhere, even near traders and bases. A red map marker follows the boss. Turn it off for normal play.
Tick and apply: one Nemesis PDA message is sent at once, with the banner icon and the PDA sound. With Debug logs on, the console says whether it went out. The box unticks itself.
Force a boss in the next hunt
For testing. Tick and apply: the emission boss comes now, even without an emission. A running hunt is called off for him. Get indoors to see the haunted exits. The box unticks itself.

Tick and apply before you remove the mod: any running hunt is called off, every Nemesis squad is removed from the world, and no new hunt starts while the box stays ticked. A PDA message tells you when it is safe to save. Then save, remove the mod and load that save. Untick it to let the hunts come back.
For testing. Tick and apply: the next hunt brings the boss, ignoring the chance, the day limit and the once-a-day rule. The box unticks itself.

Only with the Wearable Devices mod installed: when a hunt spawns, your device screens flicker at random for about 2.5 seconds. When the boss spawns, they also go black for 2 seconds after it. Without that mod this does nothing. Default on.
Write Nemesis diagnostic and error lines to the console. Leave this off unless you are tracking a problem. Lines that start with an exclamation mark are errors.
In-game days before the first hunt of a new game (or after installing the mod). Default 12.
In-game hours after a hunt ends before the next one can start. 0 = as soon as possible. Default 24.
If you survive this many in-game hours, the hunters give up and teleport away, and the next hunt is not stronger. Default 6.
A named hunter breaks off and teleports away when his health drops this low. It gets lower each cycle, so he fights longer every time. The boss never retreats. Default 25.

Each hunt you beat makes the next one stronger. That step is called a cycle. This sets how much stronger each cycle is: higher means he takes less damage and retreats later. 1.0 = no growth. Default 1.1.
The most the hunters can ever scale up, however many hunts you beat. Higher = tougher late hunts. Default 3.

How many more of their shots hit you at range than a normal stalker with the same weapon, in percent. Named hunters get this value, regular squad members half of it, and the boss this value plus 15. 0 turns it off. Default 20.

How much less damage the regular squad members take, from every hit: yours, other NPCs' and mutants'. Named hunters and the boss have their own protection (escalation and armour) and are not affected. It does not grow with the cycle. 0 makes them normal stalkers. Default 10.
Halve escalation when a hunter kills you
If a hunter kills you, the escalation is halved (cycle 8 becomes 4, never below 1), even when you reload a save. Default on.
Tick and apply to set the hunts back to their starting strength (cycle 1) right now. The box unticks itself.
How fast named hunters' armour catches up with yours. 0 = normal (full after about 10 hunts). Higher = faster, lower = slower. Regular squad members are not affected. Default 0.
How much higher than yours a named hunter's ballistic rating (BR) can get. Default 0.20. 1.0 = almost bulletproof.

The most of a hit's damage (yours or an NPC's) a named hunter or the boss can ever shrug off, however escalation, BR mitigation and boss toughness stack. At 80 they always take at least a fifth of it, so a long run never becomes unwinnable. Default 80.
How much more damage, in percent, a named hunter's armour can block than yours. Default 25. He never blocks more than 90 percent.
Turn on only if you use the Obrien GAMMA Overhaul mod. It makes hunters read your armour the way that mod does. Default off.

Nemesis stalkers you kill are not looted by NPCs. With AlifePlus installed, its own "reserve own kills" option decides (its range and time apply), and nothing is reserved while that option is off. Without AlifePlus a body stays yours for 2 in-game hours, or until you have been more than 150 m away from it for 3 minutes. Off by default: NPCs may loot them.

On the newest demonized exes, hunters use new engine features where they help: named hunters and the boss prefer you as their target and turn on whoever shoots them, and a retreating hunter is held in place by the engine for his teleport. On older exes, or with this off, the mod's own way is used. Default on.

How strongly a named hunter turns on whoever just shot him, within 60 m. On the engine's own scale, the pull toward the player when the player sees him is 900, and you count double for hunters. Higher: they turn on NPC attackers more readily. 0 leaves it to the engine. Needs Latest exe AI features and the newest demonized exes. Default 900.
The same for the boss. Kept low so he fights back but stays on you; for 5 seconds after you hurt him he ignores other NPCs anyway. 0 leaves it to the engine. Default 300.
On: when a hunter loses track of you, he searches where he last saw or heard you, and finds you again after 60 seconds. Off: he always knows where you are. Default on.

Extra squad members approach from the sides on clear lanes instead of running straight at you, and those carrying sniper rifles stop short and take a firing position. Named hunters still come straight for you. Default on.
Before teleporting away, a hurt hunter first flees away from you to cover (or, without cover, along a clear lane) for up to 4 seconds. He cannot be hurt while he runs. Default on.

Named hunters turn invisible while they stalk you from more than 30 m, and reappear when they fight, get within 15 m or take a hit that does damage. At most once every 20 seconds. While cloaked, other stalkers ignore them. Uses the same invisible model as the teleport. Experimental: a held weapon may stay visible. Default on.
Hunters stop chasing and start fighting when they see you, or any other enemy, this close. Default 70.
Hunters (the emission boss too) never spawn closer to you than this. Default 70.
The farthest from you a hunt (the emission boss too) can spawn. Default 140.
Relative chance the hunt is only the hunter. These five sliders are weights, not percents, so they do not need to add up to 100. Default 50.
Relative chance he brings one extra normal stalker. The extra can be killed. Default 25.
Relative chance of two extras with him. Default 14.
Relative chance of three extras with him. Default 10.
Relative chance of four extras with him. Default 6. Set a weight to 0 to stop that squad size.

Chance that each extra squad member is another named hunter instead of a normal stalker. Named hunters carry a rank in their name, are hard to kill and retreat when hurt. 0 = only the leader is named, 100 = the whole squad. Default 25.

On: hunts in rookie areas are smaller (Cordon and Swamps: at most 2 hunters; Garbage, Dark Valley and similar: at most 3), and in late areas extras are more often named hunters (+10 in Red Forest, Radar and similar; +20 in Pripyat, Jupiter, Zaton and the CNPP). Boss hunts are not affected. Default on.
